key: The seven milk a single cow; the two set other five to work, On the stream’s loud-resounding bank.
s: Midway through a hymn to Agni, the verse speaks in numbers; Sāyaṇa, on 8.61.7, reads the seven as priests milking the one gharma of the hot-milk rite, and two of them, the adhvaryu priests, as directing five others, the sacrificer among them.

evidence.words: "अभिष्टवे घर्मदाहे ‘ दुहन्ति सप्त ' इत्येषा … “सप्त ऋत्विजः “एकां घर्मं “दुहन्ति । तेषां मध्ये "द्वा द्वौ प्रतिप्रस्थातारावध्वर्यू “पञ्च अन्यान् “उप "सृजतः प्रयोजयतः । के ते पञ्च त उच्यन्ते । यजमानं ब्रह्माणं होतारमाग्नीध्रं प्रस्तोतारमिति । … "यज्ञस्य घर्मयागस्य साधनभूते … गवाजयोः पयसी “मही महती बहुले अपेक्षिते अत उपावतम् । गौरजाया अप्युपलक्षकः अजापयसोऽपि महावीरे सेचनीयत्वात्।
evidence.gloss: (Sāyaṇa, closing 8.72.6:) At the praise during the gharma-milking, this verse, “duhanti sapta”. … (on 8.72.7:) The seven officiating priests milk the one gharma. Among them the two, the pratiprasthātṛ and the adhvaryu, both adhvaryus, set five others to work, employ them. Who are those five? The sacrificer (yajamāna), the brahman, the hotṛ, the āgnīdhra and the prastotṛ. … (on 8.72.12:) of the sacrifice, that is of the gharma-rite, being its means … the milks of cow and goat, great and plentiful; the cow stands for the goat too, since goat’s milk also is to be poured into the mahāvīra (pot). [Separately, in English and in Cowell’s hand, not Sāyaṇa’s words: Wilson vol. 5, note 1, gives the same seven and five.]

reason: The problem holds on both counts. Reopened packet.js veda 88 (--verse 8.61.6, 8.61.7, 8.61.10, 8.61.12): Sāyaṇa on 8.61.7 says only सप्त ऋत्विजः एकां घर्मं दुहन्ति; the gloss of the one as an earthen vessel for boiling milk is Cowell’s note 1 in Wilson vol. 5 (Wilson’s manuscript ends in 8.44), and in Sāyaṇa the pot is the mahāvīra (8.61.10 to 12). Replaced the appositive with the critic’s wording, “the one gharma of the hot-milk rite”, which Sāyaṇa’s own words carry: he assigns this verse to the abhiṣṭava at the gharma-milking (अभिष्टवे घर्मदाहे, closing 8.61.6), names the rite घर्मयाग (8.61.12), and has cow’s and goat’s milk poured into the mahāvīra (8.61.12); hot-milk is the plain English of gharma as a rite name. Place changed from “commentary on 8.61.7” to “on 8.61.7”. Evidence is now Sāyaṇa’s Sanskrit alone, each piece copied by machine from the packet (the Wikisource text prints घर्मदाहे); Cowell’s note is relabelled as his and kept out of the evidence words. Key, ref, at, commentator, the priests reading and src unchanged. 42 words; verse.js ok; entry-check ok.
